presets.title: Survey the level before writing playtests
presets.summary: Learn the player start, actor classes, controls and whether a target is reachable, so later tests name real things.

placeholders.name: target
placeholders.label: Target actor
placeholders.hint: An actor label, name, tag or class the player should reach

presets.prompt:
Survey {{level}} so later playtests use real names. Change nothing in the level.
1. hyper_memory_recall with query "playtest {{target}}": past checks, class names and gotchas.
2. hyper_verify_calibrate with bMeasure false: report limit, the number of cases one batch may hold on this machine.
3. One hyper_verify_run (deadlineSeconds 30) with a single case named survey: a Survey step with target {{target}}, then a Capture step with text survey-start.
4. From the Survey evidence list: where the player starts (cm), the camera, the actor census by class, the controls with their keys (Move, Jump, Interact, Fire...), the player's health property, and the distance to {{target}} and whether the navmesh reaches it.
5. Report a table with PASS/FAIL rows: player found, controls found, {{target}} exists, {{target}} reachable, each with its evidence line. Show the capture on its own line as ![start view](path). If {{target}} is not found, list the closest class names from the census instead of guessing.

presets.title: Prove a pickup adds score and disappears
presets.summary: Walk the bot to a pickup, check it vanishes and the score rises by the right amount, with a screenshot as proof.

placeholders.name: pickup
placeholders.label: Pickup actor
placeholders.hint: Label, name, tag or class of the pickup

placeholders.name: score_owner
placeholders.label: Score owner
placeholders.hint: PlayerState, GameState, GameMode or an actor label

presets.prompt:
Prove in Play In Editor that picking up {{pickup}} in {{level}} adds {{points}} to {{score_owner}}.{{score_property}} and removes the pickup. Change nothing in the level.
1. hyper_playtest_run with a fresh operationId, mode StartInProcess, teardown StopOwnedSession, wholeTimeoutMs 120000. Bot steps, each with a stepId and timeoutMs up to 30000: Survey target {{pickup}}; Sample target {{score_owner}} property {{score_property}} seconds 0.5 (the starting score); MoveTo target {{pickup}} radius 50 timeoutSeconds 15; WaitUntil until AssertGone target {{pickup}} timeoutSeconds 3; AssertProperty target {{score_owner}} property {{score_property}} compare == value {{points}}; Capture text after-pickup.
2. hyper_operation_wait with that operationId, timeoutMs 120000 and bWaitThroughApproval true.
3. hyper_playtest_status with pageSize 64: read every step's evidence.
4. If the starting score was not 0, run once more with the expected value set to start + {{points}}.
5. Report a PASS/FAIL table: reached the pickup, pickup gone, score rose by {{points}}, each with its evidence line. Open the capture and show it on its own line as ![after pickup](path). For a failed step give its code (stuck, not_found, assertion_failed) and what the bot saw.

presets.title: Check a door opens when the player walks up
presets.summary: Walk to a door, interact, and prove its open flag flips in time, recorded as an MP4 with each step drawn over the game.

placeholders.name: door
placeholders.label: Door actor
placeholders.hint: Label, name, tag or class of the door

placeholders.name: open_property
placeholders.label: Open flag
placeholders.hint: The Blueprint variable that is true when the door is open

presets.prompt:
Prove that {{door}} in {{level}} opens for the player, and record it for review. Change nothing in the level.
1. hyper_playtest_run with a fresh operationId, mode StartInProcess, teardown StopOwnedSession, bRecordVideo true, videoFps 15. Bot steps, each with a stepId and timeoutMs: Survey target {{door}}; AssertProperty target {{door}} property {{open_property}} compare == value false; MoveTo target {{door}} radius 150 timeoutSeconds 15; Interact target {{door}}; WaitUntil until AssertProperty, target {{door}}, property {{open_property}}, compare ==, value true, timeoutSeconds {{open_seconds}}; Wait seconds 1; Capture text door-open.
2. hyper_operation_wait (timeoutMs 120000, bWaitThroughApproval true), then hyper_playtest_status with pageSize 64.
3. Report a PASS/FAIL table: closed at start, player reached the door, opened within {{open_seconds}} s, each with its evidence line. Show the capture on its own line as ![door open](path) and give the playtest.mp4 path from the video evidence item.
4. On a failure, name the step, its code and what the bot saw (distance, value). Do not change the door: this is a test, not a fix.

presets.title: Verify a feature's requirements in one minute
presets.summary: Split acceptance criteria into one bot case each, play them all at once in copies of the level, and judge each from evidence.

placeholders.name: requirements
placeholders.label: Requirements
placeholders.default: the coin adds 10 to the score and disappears; the door opens when the player walks up to it; the lava pit hurts the player
placeholders.hint: Each requirement one observable thing, separated by semicolons

presets.prompt:
Verify these requirements in {{level}}: {{requirements}}. Follow the verify skill. Nothing in the level changes, and unsaved edits are included.
1. hyper_memory_recall with the feature's key words for class names and past results. hyper_verify_calibrate with bMeasure false for limit.
2. Split the requirements into checks, each one observable thing with one pass condition. If a name is unknown, first run hyper_verify_run with one case holding a Survey step.
3. Write one case per check, named after the requirement in kebab-case, timeoutSeconds 20: MoveTo, Interact, WaitUntil and Play steps as needed, ending with the Assert step or Play goal that proves it, plus a Capture where a picture helps. No UI or AssertOnScreen steps.
4. One hyper_verify_run with every case (deadlineSeconds 60, at most limit cases; further checks go in later batches).
5. Judge each case from its evidence alone: PASS (it holds), FAIL (a game bug) or INCONCLUSIVE (the case could not tell). Rewrite an inconclusive case once and run it again.
6. Report a table: requirement, verdict, the evidence line it rests on. Show pictures on their own lines as ![case](path).

presets.title: Check a level can be finished from start to goal
presets.summary: A bot plays like a person to the goal and collects every pickup, writing maps that show where the level blocks a player.

placeholders.name: goal
placeholders.label: Goal actor
placeholders.hint: Label, name, tag or class of the goal

placeholders.name: collectible
placeholders.label: Collectibles
placeholders.hint: A tag or class naming every collectible

placeholders.name: skill_level
placeholders.label: Bot skill (0-1)
placeholders.hint: 0 plays like a new player, 1 like a skilled one

presets.prompt:
Prove a player can finish {{level}}: reach {{goal}} and collect every {{collectible}}. Change nothing.
1. hyper_level_design_validate with bCapturePreview true: navmesh routes from each start marker to each goal marker, plus the top-down preview. Routes need the blockout's start and goal markers; with none, report the route row as INFO. If the level_design pack is unavailable, say so and continue with the bot alone.
2. One hyper_verify_run (deadlineSeconds 60) with three cases, timeoutSeconds 50 each: reach-goal: Play goal Reach target {{goal}} radius 200 skill {{skill_level}} seed 1 timeoutSeconds 45; reach-goal-seed2: the same with seed 2; collect-all: Play goal Collect target {{collectible}} skill {{skill_level}} seed 1 timeoutSeconds 45, then Capture text collected.
3. Read each Play result: time taken, jumps, obstacles gone round, stuck spots (cm) and, for Collect, the ones left behind.
4. Report a PASS/FAIL table: route found, goal reached with both seeds, all collected, each with its evidence line. Open every Play map and show it on its own line as ![map](path), with the validate preview the same way.
5. For each stuck spot give its location and the likely cause you can see on the map (a gap, a step too high, a blocked doorway). Do not fix the level.

presets.title: Find where players get stuck or fall out
presets.summary: Several bots explore the level at once; merge their maps into a list of stuck spots and falls so you know where to fix collision.

placeholders.name: explore_seconds
placeholders.label: Seconds each bot explores
placeholders.hint: At most 50

presets.prompt:
Find where players get trapped or fall out of {{level}}. Change nothing.
1. hyper_verify_calibrate with bMeasure false; use the smaller of {{bots}} and limit as the case count.
2. One hyper_verify_run (deadlineSeconds 60) with that many cases named explore-1, explore-2 and on, each with timeoutSeconds {{explore_seconds}} plus 5: Play goal Explore seconds {{explore_seconds}} with a different seed per case, then Capture text explore-N-end.
3. Merge the results: how many 4 m squares each bot visited, and every stuck spot and fall with its location in cm. Treat spots within 300 cm of each other as one place, and count how many bots hit it.
4. Report a table: place (x, y, z), stuck or fall, bots affected out of N. PASS when no bot fell and no place trapped two or more bots, otherwise FAIL. Show each Play map on its own line as ![explore N](path).
5. For the top three places, say what the map shows there (a gap, a ledge, a tight corner) and what a designer should check. Fix nothing.

presets.title: Playtest a combat encounter as new and skilled players
presets.summary: Bots at two skill levels fight the encounter; compare wins, accuracy, damage and health left against your targets.

placeholders.name: enemies
placeholders.label: Enemies
placeholders.hint: A tag or class naming every enemy in the encounter

placeholders.name: health_property
placeholders.label: Health property
placeholders.hint: Property path the bot reads health from

presets.prompt:
Playtest the {{enemies}} encounter in {{level}} as a new and a skilled player. Change nothing.
1. hyper_memory_recall with query "combat {{enemies}} damage" for known damage-path gotchas. hyper_verify_calibrate with bMeasure false for limit.
2. hyper_verify_run (deadlineSeconds 60), timeoutSeconds 50 per case: new-1 to new-3: Play goal Defeat target {{enemies}} skill 0.2 healthProperty {{health_property}} timeoutSeconds 45 with seeds 1 to 3; skilled-1 to skilled-3: the same with skill 0.8. End each case with a Capture. If limit is under 6, run the skilled cases as a second batch.
3. For each case read: passed, or its code (defeated, no_damage, no_attack_action); shots and shots on target; damage dealt and taken; health left; time.
4. Report a table per skill level: wins of 3, mean accuracy, mean health left, mean time. PASS rows: skilled wins 3 of 3; the new player wins at least {{new_wins}} of 3; no case ends no_damage or no_attack_action. Show each Play map on its own line as ![case](path).
5. A no_damage result is a bug in the damage path: name the case and its evidence. Do not change enemy or weapon values.

presets.title: Prove the HUD shows damage when the player is hurt
presets.summary: Walk into a hazard, confirm health drops, and check the HUD widget's text changes on screen, with captures before and after.

placeholders.name: hud_widget
placeholders.label: HUD text widget
placeholders.hint: UserWidget.WidgetName of the text that shows health

placeholders.name: hud_full_text
placeholders.label: HUD text at full health
placeholders.hint: Exactly what the widget reads at full health

presets.prompt:
Prove that taking damage from {{hazard}} in {{level}} lowers health and updates {{hud_widget}} on screen. Change nothing.
1. hyper_ui_inspect on the HUD's Widget Blueprint with bIncludeTree true: confirm the widget named in {{hud_widget}} exists. If the ui_slate_mvvm pack is unavailable, say so and continue.
2. hyper_playtest_run with a fresh operationId, mode StartInProcess, teardown StopOwnedSession. Bot steps with stepIds and timeoutMs: UiAssert widget {{hud_widget}} compare == value {{hud_full_text}}; Capture text hud-before; MoveTo target {{hazard}} radius 50 timeoutSeconds 15; WaitUntil until AssertProperty target Player property {{health_property}} compare < value {{max_health}} timeoutSeconds 5; UiAssert widget {{hud_widget}} compare != value {{hud_full_text}}; Capture text hud-after.
3. hyper_operation_wait (timeoutMs 120000, bWaitThroughApproval true), then hyper_playtest_status with pageSize 64.
4. Report a PASS/FAIL table: HUD full at start, player hurt (the health read), HUD changed, each with its evidence line. Open both captures and show them on their own lines as ![before](path) and ![after](path), and say whether the number on screen matches the health read.

presets.title: Test a door replicates to clients and late joiners
presets.summary: Host and client play in one editor; the host opens the door, and checks on the client and a late joiner prove it replicated.
presets.prompt:
Prove {{door}} in {{level}} replicates its open state. Change nothing in the level.
1. hyper_playtest_run with a fresh operationId, mode StartInProcess, teardown LeaveSessionRunning, netMode ListenServer, numPlayers 2, bRecordVideo true. Steps, each with a stepId and timeoutMs: host (pieInstance 0) Bot MoveTo target {{door}} radius 150 timeoutSeconds 15; host Bot Interact target {{door}}; client (pieInstance 1) Bot WaitUntil until AssertProperty target {{door}} property {{open_property}} compare == value true timeoutSeconds 3; kind JoinPlayer with timeoutMs 20000; late joiner (pieInstance 2) Bot AssertProperty target {{door}} property {{open_property}} == true; pieInstance 1 Bot Capture text client-view.
2. hyper_operation_wait (timeoutMs 120000, bWaitThroughApproval true), then hyper_playtest_status with pageSize 64.
3. While play still runs, hyper_pie_query: list each world's pieInstance and net mode, proving one host and two clients. Then stop play with Epic's StopPIE.
4. Report a PASS/FAIL table: host opened it, client saw it within 3 s, late joiner saw it, three worlds present. Show the client capture on its own line as ![client view](path) and give the video path. A failure on a client but not the host means the flag or the door's movement does not replicate: say which.

presets.title: Balance-check a 1v1 duel with two bot players
presets.summary: Two local bots duel at different skill levels across several seeds; report who wins, accuracy and time to kill.
presets.prompt:
Balance-check the 1v1 duel in {{level}}. Change nothing.
1. hyper_verify_calibrate with bMeasure false; run the smaller of 4 and limit cases.
2. One hyper_verify_run (deadlineSeconds 60). Each case duel-N (timeoutSeconds 50): AddPlayer at location ({{distance_cm}}, 0, 100) in world cm (if the start is far from the origin, use a point {{distance_cm}} cm in front of it); Wait seconds 0.5; Play goal Defeat target Player0 playerIndex 1 skill {{skill_b}} bBackground true timeoutSeconds 40 seed N; Play goal Defeat target Player1 skill {{skill_a}} timeoutSeconds 40 seed N; Capture text duel-N.
3. For each case read who won (passed means Player0, defeated means Player1), shots, hits, damage dealt and taken, health left and time.
4. Report a table per case and a summary. PASS rows: the player with skill {{skill_a}} wins at least 3 of 4; mean time to kill between {{ttk_min}} and {{ttk_max}} s; no no_damage or no_attack_action. Show each Play map on its own line as ![duel N](path).
5. Say what the numbers suggest (one-sided, too fast, too slow) without changing any weapon or health values.

presets.title: Measure walk speed, stopping and jump against targets
presets.summary: Hold the move input, sample the speed, release, and jump; compare walk speed and stopping with the pawn's settings or your targets.

placeholders.name: walk_speed
placeholders.label: Target walk speed (cm/s)
placeholders.hint: A number, or pawn to use the pawn's WalkSpeed

presets.prompt:
Measure movement feel in {{level}} against the design targets. Change nothing.
1. hyper_input_inspect on the player's mapping context with bIncludeMappings true: confirm {{move_action}} and the jump action exist and what they are bound to. If the enhanced_input pack is unavailable, use a Survey step's control list instead.
2. hyper_level_design_inspect: the pawn's WalkSpeed and JumpHeight. JumpHeight is the jump target; WalkSpeed is the speed target when {{walk_speed}} is pawn. If the level_design pack is unavailable, say so and check only what has a number.
3. One hyper_verify_run (deadlineSeconds 40) with three cases: walk-speed: Hold inputAction {{move_action}} value 0,1 seconds 3 bBackground true; Wait seconds 1; Sample seconds 1. stop: Hold {{move_action}} value 0,1 seconds 2; Sample seconds 1. jump: Jump timeoutSeconds 3; Capture text jump.
4. From the evidence read the steady walk speed (cm/s), the lowest speed in the second after release, and the jump height the Jump step reports (cm).
5. Report a PASS/FAIL table: walk speed within {{tolerance}}% of the target; speed reaches 0 within 1 s of release; the jump lands and its height is within {{tolerance}}% of JumpHeight. Quote each evidence line, and show the capture on its own line as ![jump](path).

presets.title: Record a reviewable video of a quest step
presets.summary: Play a short scripted path through one quest step and save an MP4 with every step's result drawn on it, plus a timeline.

placeholders.name: npc
placeholders.label: Quest giver
placeholders.hint: Label, name or class of the NPC to talk to

presets.prompt:
Record a reviewable video of the quest step in {{level}}: talk to {{npc}}, then pick up {{objective}}. Change nothing in the level.
1. hyper_playtest_run with a fresh operationId, mode StartInProcess, teardown StopOwnedSession, bRecordVideo true, videoFps {{fps}}. Bot steps, each with a stepId and timeoutMs: MoveTo target {{npc}} radius 200 timeoutSeconds 20; Interact target {{npc}}; Wait seconds 2; Capture text dialogue; MoveTo target {{objective}} radius 100 timeoutSeconds 20; Interact target {{objective}}; WaitUntil until AssertGone target {{objective}} timeoutSeconds 3; Capture text objective-taken.
2. hyper_operation_wait with timeoutMs 120000 and bWaitThroughApproval true.
3. hyper_playtest_status with pageSize 64: the last evidence item is the video, with playtest.mp4 under Saved/HyperAIStudio/Playtests/<operationId>/ and timeline.json beside it.
4. Report a PASS/FAIL table, one row per step, with its evidence line and its start time from the timeline. Give the video and timeline paths, and show both captures on their own lines as ![dialogue](path) and ![objective](path).
5. If a step fails, the run stops there: report the code and what the bot saw, and still give the video of what was recorded.

presets.title: Check an enemy AI chases and then loses the player
presets.summary: Prove the enemy closes in once the player is near, and gives up after the player flees out of range.

placeholders.name: ai_asset
placeholders.label: Behavior Tree or AI Controller
placeholders.hint: Object path of the enemy's Behavior Tree or AI Controller Blueprint

presets.prompt:
Test that {{enemy}} in {{level}} chases the player and then loses them. Change nothing.
1. hyper_gameplay_ai_inspect with assetPaths [{{ai_asset}}] and bIncludeDetails true: note the blackboard keys and chase and search branches, or the controller's senses. If the gameplay_ai pack is unavailable, say so and continue with the bot alone.
2. One hyper_verify_run (deadlineSeconds 60) with two cases:
- chases (timeoutSeconds 30): Survey target {{enemy}}; MoveTo target {{enemy}} radius 800 timeoutSeconds 15; WaitUntil until AssertNear target {{enemy}} other Player radius {{chase_radius}} timeoutSeconds 6; Capture text caught.
- loses-player (timeoutSeconds 50): MoveTo target {{enemy}} radius 800 timeoutSeconds 15; Play goal Flee target {{enemy}} range {{flee_range}} seconds {{flee_seconds}}; Sample target {{enemy}} seconds 2; Capture text escaped.
3. From the evidence read how fast the enemy closed in, the distance when the flee ended, and the enemy's speed and distance moved afterwards.
4. Report a PASS/FAIL table: enemy reaches {{chase_radius}} cm within 6 s; player escapes (no caught code); enemy stops pursuing (speed near 0 or moving away). Show the captures and the Play map on their own lines as ![case](path).

presets.title: Regression-test a Blueprint fix in play
presets.summary: Compile the fixed Blueprint, replay the bug's steps in parallel cases, and confirm no new script errors reach the log.

placeholders.name: bug
placeholders.label: The bug that was fixed
placeholders.default: the turret keeps firing after it is destroyed

presets.prompt:
Regression-test the fix for: {{bug}}. The fixed Blueprint is {{selected_asset}}. Change nothing.
1. hyper_blueprint_compile_validate on {{selected_asset}}: call it once to preview and get the PlanHash, again with that expectedPlanHash and a fresh operationId, then hyper_operation_wait. It must compile with 0 errors.
2. hyper_log_tail with categories [LogScript, LogBlueprint], maxVerbosity warning and pageSize 1: keep its nextCursor as the mark before play. A cursor only works with the same categories and verbosity.
3. Write {{cases}} cases that replay the bug's steps from different starts or seeds, each ending with the Assert step that fails if the bug is back, then a Capture. Run them in one hyper_verify_run with deadlineSeconds 60.
4. hyper_log_tail from the mark's cursor with the same categories and maxVerbosity, and pageSize 128: list new errors and warnings (Accessed None, infinite loop) with the Blueprint and function they name.
5. Report a PASS/FAIL table: compiles clean; each case passes, with its evidence line; no new script errors. Show captures on their own lines as ![case](path). If the bug is back, say which case caught it.

presets.title: Click through a menu and check each screen opens
presets.summary: Click menu buttons through Slate in Play In Editor, assert the screen each opens and that Back returns, capturing every screen.

placeholders.name: screen_widget
placeholders.label: Widget the button should show
placeholders.hint: UserWidget.WidgetName

presets.prompt:
Click through {{menu_widget}} in {{level}} and prove {{open_button}} opens its screen and Back returns. Change nothing.
1. hyper_ui_inspect on {{menu_widget}} and on the Widget Blueprint of {{screen_widget}} with bIncludeTree true: confirm every widget name used below exists. If the ui_slate_mvvm pack is unavailable, say so and continue.
2. hyper_playtest_run with a fresh operationId, mode StartInProcess, teardown StopOwnedSession. Bot steps with stepIds and timeoutMs: Wait seconds 1; UiAssert widget {{menu_widget}}.{{open_button}}; Capture text menu; UiClick widget {{menu_widget}}.{{open_button}}; Wait seconds 0.5; UiAssert widget {{screen_widget}}; Capture text screen; UiClick widget {{back_button}}; Wait seconds 0.5; UiAssert widget {{menu_widget}}.{{open_button}}; Capture text back.
3. hyper_operation_wait (timeoutMs 120000, bWaitThroughApproval true), then hyper_playtest_status with pageSize 64.
4. Report a PASS/FAIL table: menu shown, button clicked, screen shown, back returns, each with its evidence line. Show the three captures on their own lines as ![menu](path), ![screen](path) and ![back](path). A widget_not_found code names a widget that was not on screen: report which.

presets.title: Check attacks go where the player aims
presets.summary: Aim an attack at an enemy the way the game reads aim (cursor, stick or view), and prove the game's own aim and the hit went that way.

placeholders.name: enemy
placeholders.label: Enemy
placeholders.hint: Label, name, tag or class of the enemy to attack

placeholders.name: attack
placeholders.label: Attack input action
placeholders.hint: The input action that attacks, such as IA_Attack or IA_PrimaryAbility

presets.prompt:
Check that an attack in {{level}} goes where the player aims. Change nothing in the level.
1. hyper_playtest_run with a fresh operationId, mode StartInProcess, teardown StopOwnedSession, bRecordVideo true. Bot steps, each with a stepId and timeoutMs: Survey target {{enemy}}; MoveTo target {{enemy}} radius 500 timeoutSeconds 15; AimAt target {{enemy}} aim Auto seconds 0.5; Press inputAction {{attack}} target {{enemy}} aim Auto; Wait seconds 1; Capture text after-attack.
2. hyper_operation_wait with timeoutMs 120000 and bWaitThroughApproval true, then hyper_playtest_status with pageSize 64.
3. From the AimAt and Press evidence, report how the bot aimed (cursor, stick or look) and why, the cursor's point in the window, and each reading of the game's own aim (GetAimWorldLocation, GetAimDirection, GetAimDirectionFlat) with how far off it was.
4. Report a PASS/FAIL table: the game's aim on {{enemy}}, the attack pressed while aimed, and any health or hit change the Survey and capture show. Give the video path; the video draws each aim as a ring and a line.
5. If a step fails aim_off_target, the game aims some other way: run the same steps again with aim Cursor, then Stick, then Look, and say which one passes. If none passes, the game's aim code ignores its input: name the step and its evidence.

presets.title: Find how the game reads the player's aim
presets.summary: Aim at a target by cursor, stick and view in turn, and report which one the game's own aim follows, before writing combat tests.

placeholders.name: target
placeholders.label: Something to aim at
placeholders.hint: Label, name, tag or class of an actor in view of the player

presets.prompt:
Find how {{level}} reads its player's aim. Change nothing in the level.
1. hyper_playtest_run with a fresh operationId, mode StartInProcess, teardown StopOwnedSession: a Survey step with target {{target}}, then AimAt target {{target}} aim Auto seconds 0.5. Follow it with hyper_operation_wait (timeoutMs 120000, bWaitThroughApproval true) and hyper_playtest_status (pageSize 64).
2. Run the same two steps three more times, once each with aim Cursor, Stick and Look. A run that fails aim_off_target shows the game does not aim that way.
3. Report a table with one row per aim: passed or its code, and the game's own aim readings with how far off they were. Quote Auto's reason, and say whether Auto chose the aim that passes.
4. If the game has no GetAimWorldLocation, GetAimDirection or GetAimDirectionFlat, every aim passes without a reading: say so, and suggest checking an attack's hit instead.

presets.title: Survey the level: reachable ground, stuck spots and falls
presets.summary: One SurveyLevel step maps what a player can reach, films it, and finds where it gets stuck or falls out.

placeholders.name: cells
placeholders.label: Grid cells a side
placeholders.hint: 4 to 48; more is finer and slower

placeholders.name: walk_seconds
placeholders.label: Seconds of walking
placeholders.hint: Short walks that look for stuck spots and falls

presets.prompt:
Survey {{level}} for what a player can reach. Change nothing in the level.
1. hyper_verify_run (deadlineSeconds 60) with one case named level-survey, timeoutSeconds 55: Wait seconds 0.5, then SurveyLevel with value "{{cells}}", seconds {{walk_seconds}}, timeoutSeconds 50 and text level-survey.
2. Read the step's detail and open coverage.json and overview.png in the folder its file names.
3. Report a table with PASS/FAIL rows: reachable share of the ground at least 80% (with the counts), no fall out of the world, no stuck spot, method (navmesh or ground). List every stuck spot and fall with its location in cm.
4. Show the overview on its own line as ![overview](path) and link survey.mp4. Say what the red (unreachable) areas look like on the overview and whether a player is meant to reach them. Fix nothing.

presets.title: Check an ability through GAS while playing
presets.summary: Press an ability and prove it ran, cost what it should, and applied its effect and tags.

placeholders.name: input_action
placeholders.label: Input action
placeholders.hint: The action that triggers the ability

placeholders.name: ability
placeholders.label: Ability class
placeholders.hint: Such as GA_Fireball

placeholders.name: cost_attribute
placeholders.label: Cost attribute
placeholders.hint: The attribute it spends

placeholders.name: effect
placeholders.label: Effect on the target
placeholders.hint: Such as GE_Burning

placeholders.name: target
placeholders.label: Target
placeholders.hint: An actor label, tag or class

presets.prompt:
Prove {{ability}} works in {{level}} by playing it. Change nothing in the level.
1. hyper_playtest_run (mode StartInProcess, bRecordVideo true) with Bot steps: AssertAbility target Player property {{ability}} (granted); AssertAttribute target Player property {{cost_attribute}} compare > value 0; Press inputAction {{input_action}} with target {{target}} and aim Auto; WaitUntil AssertAbility property {{ability}} value active (timeoutSeconds 2); WaitUntil AssertEffect target {{target}} property {{effect}} (timeoutSeconds 5); AssertAttribute target Player property {{cost_attribute}} compare < with the value read before; Capture.
2. hyper_operation_wait with bWaitThroughApproval true, then hyper_playtest_status for the evidence.
3. Report a PASS/FAIL table, one row per check with its evidence line (granted abilities, attribute values, effect stacks). Show the capture and link the video. A no_ability_system result means GAS is not on that actor: say where it is instead.

presets.title: Play an 8-player session with late joiners
presets.summary: A listen server, its clients and late joiners, each with a bot, checking what replicated to every one.

placeholders.name: players
placeholders.label: Players at the start
placeholders.hint: 2 to 6; late joiners make up the rest of 8

placeholders.name: target
placeholders.label: Replicated actor
placeholders.hint: An actor every player should see

placeholders.name: property
placeholders.label: Its replicated property
placeholders.hint: Such as bOpen

presets.prompt:
Check {{target}}.{{property}} replicates to every player in {{level}}, with 8 players. Change nothing in the level.
1. hyper_playtest_run with mode StartInProcess, netMode ListenServer, numPlayers {{players}}, bRecordVideo true and wholeTimeoutMs 240000. Steps: a Bot MoveTo {{target}} radius 150 as the host (pieInstance 0); then for each client 1 to {{players}} minus 1 a Bot WaitUntil AssertProperty target {{target}} property {{property}} compare == value true with that pieInstance; then JoinPlayer steps until there are 8 players, each followed by the same WaitUntil on the new instance.
2. If it is refused with not_enough_memory, rerun with the player count it names and say so.
3. hyper_operation_wait with bWaitThroughApproval true, then hyper_playtest_status (pageSize 64).
4. Report a table, one row per player (host, clients, late joiners): PASS or FAIL with its evidence line. Link the video.

presets.title: Playtest on phones over the local network
presets.summary: Stream Play In Editor to phones with Pixel Streaming 2, show the QR code, and record the bot playing.

placeholders.name: viewers
placeholders.label: Viewers
placeholders.hint: 1 to 8 phones at once

presets.prompt:
Set up a phone playtest of {{level}} for up to {{viewers}} phones on this network.
1. hyper_phone_playtest_start with bDryRun true and maxViewers {{viewers}}. If it is refused, report why (plugin not enabled, player page missing, a public address) and stop.
2. Tell the user the URL, the ports and the exposure line, then call it again with bDryRun false; hyper_operation_wait with bWaitThroughApproval true.
3. hyper_phone_playtest_status: show the QR code on its own line as ![scan to play](qrCodePng) and the URL in a code block.
4. When the user says the phones are connected, run hyper_playtest_run (bRecordVideo true) with a Survey step and a Play Explore step of 30 seconds, so the phones watch the bot play; then report the viewer count from hyper_phone_playtest_status and link the video.
5. Leave it running for the user; say hyper_phone_playtest_stop ends it.

presets.title: Drive the player's input in play and measure the result
presets.summary: Hold Enhanced Input actions for set times with Epic's InputToolset58 during play, and read where the pawn went and what it did.
presets.prompt:
In {{level}}, press the player's Enhanced Input actions as a real player would (hold forward for {{seconds}} s, then jump) through its mapping context, and measure how far the pawn walked and how high it jumped. Change nothing in the level. Use Epic's `InputToolset.InputToolset58`; if it is not listed, say so and stop. On this engine every argument of these toolsets is required: pass empty strings, 0 or null for the ones you do not need.
1. hyper_input_inspect `{{move_action}}` and `{{jump_action}}`: their value types (Axis2D, Boolean) and the mapping context that holds them.
2. If Play In Editor is not running, start it with hyper_playtest_run (mode StartInProcess, teardown LeaveSessionRunning, one Bot step Wait seconds 2) and hyper_operation_wait with bWaitThroughApproval true. hyper_pie_query for the world and the player's pawn; read its root component's RelativeLocation with Epic's ObjectTools get_properties.
3. InputToolset58 ApplyInput with entries [{action {{move_action}}, value 0,1,0}] (Y is forward on a usual Axis2D move) and durationSeconds {{seconds}}; when it completes, read the location again.
4. ApplyInput with [{action {{jump_action}}, value 1,0,0}] and durationSeconds 0; read the location three times over the next 0.6 s for the jump's height.
5. If ApplyInput reports no local player, play is not running in this process: say so and stop.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: distance moved forward in cm and the speed it implies (against the movement component's MaxWalkSpeed from get_properties), the jump's peak height in cm, and the pawn back on the ground. Stop play with Epic's StopPIE if you started it.

presets.title: Use cheats to reach a late area and test it
presets.summary: List the game's cheats with Epic's CheatsToolset, use them to get to an area quickly and safely, then run a short check there.

placeholders.name: check
placeholders.label: What to check there
placeholders.default: the boss door opens when the player walks up

presets.prompt:
Get to {{destination}} in {{level}} fast with cheats and check that {{check}}. Change nothing in the level. Use Epic's `CheatsToolset.CheatsToolset`; if it is not listed, say so and stop. On this engine every argument of these toolsets is required: pass empty strings, 0 or null for the ones you do not need.
1. If Play In Editor is not running, start it with hyper_playtest_run (mode StartInProcess, teardown LeaveSessionRunning, one Bot step Wait seconds 2) and hyper_operation_wait with bWaitThroughApproval true. hyper_pie_query: one local player.
2. CheatsToolset ListCheats with nameFilter "": the cheats this game has, with their argument hints.
3. CallCheat God (args ""), so nothing kills the tester on the way; then BugItGo with args the three numbers of {{destination}} followed by 0 0 0, or the game's own warp cheat if it has one. If neither exists, say which cheats there are and stop.
4. CallCheat Walk, so the check runs with normal movement and collision.
5. hyper_verify_run with one case for {{check}} at {{destination}}: Survey the area, then the assert the check needs.
6. CallCheat God again to turn it off.
Reply with a PASS/FAIL table: reached {{destination}} (within 300 cm), the check itself with its evidence, and god mode off at the end; list the cheats you used. Stop play with Epic's StopPIE if you started it.
